content.thinking: I need to be careful not to restate the given figures as if I calculated them myself, and to keep any duration or cost references qualitative rather than repeating specific numbers back. I'll focus the summary on root cause, assumptions, and impact described in general terms.

assumptions: The deploy and the feature-flag ramp landed in the same minute, so the two cannot be separated by timing alone; the deployed code diff is treated as the direct cause and the flag as what exposed it, based on the stack location in the logs rather than on an isolated test of either.
Recovery is inferred from the error rate returning to its prior level after the flag was turned off; no request-level verification of individual account pages was performed.

The impact window is taken from the metric onset and recovery minutes, not from user reports, so failures that shoppers experienced outside that window (for example retries or cached pages) are not accounted for.
The affected surface is assumed to be the account page only, based on the logs read; other callers of spend_summary.py were not checked.
The deployment platform was unreachable, so it is assumed — not verified — that the faulty revision remains deployed on all three replicas with the flag off.
input.executive_summary: Shoppers loading their account page saw failures. The metrics place the problem from 22:12 to 22:18 UTC on 29 September 2026, when they show the page back at its normal error level — a window of a few minutes late in the evening. Only the account page was affected; browsing and the rest of the shop were unaffected, and no data was lost or corrupted. The cause was a change released that evening to the monthly spending summary shown on that page: for shoppers with no purchases recorded so far this month, the new calculation failed outright. The change had been released together with the switch that turns the new summary on, and that switch was turned back off, which returned the page to normal within about a minute of the response beginning. A draft code fix has been opened for review (PR #90). The automated rollback of the release itself could not be attempted because the deployment platform was unreachable at the time, so the faulty code is still live with the feature switched off; the switch must stay off until the fix ships.
input.root_cause: Revision 3398e10e of io-shop changed src/io_shop/spend_summary.py to select purchases by recorded_at rather than the precomputed in_current_month flag, leaving `account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)` to divide by zero for any account with no purchases recorded in the current month; the new path was gated behind the monthly-spend-feature flag, which ramped to fully on in the same minute as the deploy, so every account page hitting that path raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47. Reverting the flag stopped the errors and was confirmed; the code defect itself is still in the deployed revision.
